$comment: Project-scoped MCP servers. Committed, so it must never contain a secret.
IT IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE. An earlier version declared the Supabase server here
with "SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN": "${SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN}", which never
worked: Claude Code expands ${VAR} from the PROCESS environment, and that
token lives in .env.local, which only dotenv reads inside our own Node
scripts. Claude Code never opens that file. So `npm run migrate` worked and
the MCP server silently did not.
Both servers now live in user scope (~/.claude.json), which keeps the tokens
out of this repository entirely. Set them up once, per machine:
SUPABASE — run migrations and query the database in conversation.
Token: supabase.com > Account > Access Tokens.
claude mcp add supabase --scope user \
--env SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=sbp_xxx -- \
cmd /c npx -y @supabase/mcp-server-supabase@latest \
--project-ref=trrgppbjjuklcjyagdva
STITCH — generate UI designs and read them back as HTML and screenshots.
Key: stitch.withgoogle.com > profile picture > Stitch settings > API key.
claude mcp add stitch --scope user \
--env STITCH_API_KEY=xxx -- \
cmd /c npx -y @_davideast/stitch-mcp proxy
The `cmd /c` prefix is required on Windows; npx-based stdio servers fail to
spawn without it.
Restart Claude Code after either, then run /mcp to see what connected.
CLOUDFLARE is deliberately absent. CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and
CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID are already in .env.local and already drive cfFetch in
server.ts, so `npm run cf` reaches Pages with no new credential. Add the
hosted server only if you want it in conversation:
claude mcp add --transport sse cloudflare https://observability.mcp.cloudflare.com/sse
If a server ever does belong in this file — one every agent on the project
needs — it goes here WITHOUT credentials, and the operator supplies those
through their own environment.
